newsitem.title: UK: ASDA climbs as results prompt upgrades.
newsitem.headline: ASDA climbs as results prompt upgrades.

text.p: Shares in supermarket group ASDA Plc stayed higher on Thursday following better than expected annual results and as analysts upgraded earnings forecasts and stock ratings.
The shares were up 4-1/4p to 126-1/4 by 1103 GMT.
Market sources said BZW had upgraded the stock to "hold" from "sell" but analysts there declined to comment.

Earlier, ASDA turned in strong sales and 16 percent profit growth, which topped analysts expectations. Market share grew to 11 percent from 10.1 percent, whilst the price gap with competitors continued to widen.
Dealers said SBC Warburg remained buyers of the stock up to 135p and held 1998 earnings forecasts unchanged at 395 million stg.
Simon Dunn at Kleinwort Benson said he was expecting to raise his forecast from a current 380 million stg.
Kleinwort remains a strong buyer of ASDA.

"62 months of outperforming the industry is more than just a recovery," Dunn commented. "The mission to differentiate because of their bigger stores is likely to drive their spend per customer up and we see that as the key to further growth," he added. -- Elaine Hardcastle, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
